title: Finite limits of internal abelian groups are created on underlying objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. Write $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ for the category whose objects are quadruples $(M,m,e,i)$, with $m:M\times M\to M$, $e:*\to M$ and $i:M\to M$ satisfying associativity, commutativity, the two unit laws and the inverse laws as equations of morphisms; here $*$ is terminal and products have the meaning of [def-weil-category-product]. Morphisms preserve these operations. Let $U_{\mathcal C}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ forget the operations.

For every finite category $I$, every diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$ and every limiting cone $(L,(p_j)_j)$ of $U_{\mathcal C}D$, there is exactly one abelian-group-object structure on the same object $L$ making all $p_j$ group-object morphisms. With this structure the cone is limiting in $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$: the unique underlying factorization of any group-object cone is a group-object morphism. Moreover, a cone of group objects is limiting if and only if its underlying cone is limiting. Thus $U_{\mathcal C}$ creates, preserves and reflects finite limits, including the empty limit.

Let $\mathcal D$ also have finite limits, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits. Equip $FM$ with $F(m)\circ\lambda_{M,M}^{-1}$, $F(e)\circ\lambda_*^{-1}$ and $F(i)$, where $\lambda_{M,N}:F(M\times N)\to FM\times FN$ and $\lambda_*:F(*)\to *$ are the canonical comparisons. This operation transport, with $h\mapsto F(h)$ on morphisms, defines a functor $F^{\mathrm{ab}}:\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal D)$, and $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ preserves finite limits.

The arbitrary finite-limit-category formulation is agent-extracted, not a verbatim assertion of the proposition.

proof.text: Fix a finite diagram $D$ and an underlying limiting cone $(L,p_j)$ as in the statement. Write $M_j=U_{\mathcal C}D(j)$ and $(m_j,e_j,i_j)$ for its operations. Here the limit universal property means: every compatible family $t_j:T\to M_j$ has a unique factorization $u:T\to L$ with $p_ju=t_j$. For maps $a,b:T\to L$, if $p_j a=p_j b$ for every $j$, then $a=b$: both are factorizations of the same cone with vertex $T$, so the uniqueness clause of the defining limit universal property applies. We will use this equality test for $T=L$, $L\times L$, $*$ and $(L\times L)\times L$. It also applies when the diagram is empty: there is exactly one map $T\to L$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text:
For an arrow $\alpha:j\to k$ of $I$, put $d=U_{\mathcal C}D(\alpha)$, so $dp_j=p_k$. Operation preservation gives
$$d m_j(p_j\times p_j)=m_k(dp_j\times dp_j)=m_k(p_k\times p_k),\quad de_j=e_k,\quad d i_jp_j=i_kdp_j=i_kp_k.$$
Thus $m_j(p_j\times p_j)$, $e_j$, and $i_jp_j$ are cones on $U_{\mathcal C}D$ with vertices $L\times L$, $*$, and $L$, respectively. The limit supplies unique maps $m_L:L\times L\to L$, $e_L:*\to L$, and $i_L:L\to L$ with
$$p_jm_L=m_j(p_j\times p_j),\qquad p_je_L=e_j,\qquad p_ji_L=i_jp_j.$$
These equations will make every $p_j$ an operation-preserving map once the laws on $L$ are checked.

proof.text:
For the source $T=(L\times L)\times L$, let $x,y,z:T\to L$ be its three projections. For each $j$, the defining equations of step 2 and the two projection equations for pairing give
$$p_jm_L\langle m_L\langle x,y\rangle,z\rangle
=m_j\langle m_j\langle p_jx,p_jy\rangle,p_jz\rangle
=m_j\langle p_jx,m_j\langle p_jy,p_jz\rangle\rangle
=p_jm_L\langle x,m_L\langle y,z\rangle\rangle.$$
The middle equality is associativity in $M_j$; the equality test of step 1 gives associativity on $L$. For the two projections $x,y:L\times L\to L$, commutativity follows from
$$p_jm_L\langle x,y\rangle=m_j\langle p_jx,p_jy\rangle=m_j\langle p_jy,p_jx\rangle=p_jm_L\langle y,x\rangle,$$
again using that equality test. All products and pairings here have the cited product universal property.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text:
Write $!_T:T\to *$ for the unique terminal map. For every $j$ the left and right unit equations and the two inverse equations are
$$\begin{aligned}
p_jm_L\langle e_L!_L,1_L\rangle&=m_j\langle e_j!_L,p_j\rangle=p_j,\\
p_jm_L\langle 1_L,e_L!_L\rangle&=m_j\langle p_j,e_j!_L\rangle=p_j,\\
p_jm_L\langle 1_L,i_L\rangle&=m_j\langle p_j,i_jp_j\rangle=e_j!_L=p_je_L!_L,\\
p_jm_L\langle i_L,1_L\rangle&=m_j\langle i_jp_j,p_j\rangle=e_j!_L=p_je_L!_L.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $!_{M_j}p_j=!_L$ by terminal uniqueness. Step 1 therefore gives all four laws on $L$. This makes $L$ an abelian group object. If another such structure makes all $p_j$ morphisms, its three operations satisfy exactly the three equations in step 2, so limit uniqueness makes them $m_L,e_L,i_L$. Equality of proof witnesses adds no further structure data.

proof.text:
Let $(A,q_j)$ be any cone of abelian group objects. Its underlying cone factors uniquely as $q_j=p_ju$ with $u:U_{\mathcal C}A\to L$. Since $q_j$ preserves the operations, step 2 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
p_jum_A&=q_jm_A=m_j(q_j\times q_j)=p_jm_L(u\times u),\\
p_jue_A&=q_je_A=e_j=p_je_L,\\
p_jui_A&=q_ji_A=i_jq_j=p_ji_Lu.
\end{aligned}$$
Step 1 gives $um_A=m_L(u\times u)$, $ue_A=e_L$, $ui_A=i_Lu$. Hence $u$ is a group-object morphism. Equality of these morphisms is equality of underlying maps, so their uniqueness follows from the same underlying limit. This proves that the lifted cone is limiting. For any given group cone whose underlying cone is limiting, structure uniqueness in step 4 identifies its operations with this lift; hence the given cone is limiting too.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text: Conversely suppose a group-object cone $(A,q_j)$ is limiting. Choose an underlying limit $(L,p_j)$, which exists since $I$ is finite and $\mathcal C$ has finite limits, and equip it as above. Step 5 gives a group map $a:A\to L$ with $p_ja=q_j$, while the assumed group limit gives a group map $b:L\to A$ with $q_jb=p_j$. Underlying limit uniqueness gives $ab=1_L$, and group limit uniqueness gives $ba=1_A$. For any underlying cone $(T,t_j)$, let $v:T\to L$ be its unique underlying factorization. Then $bv:T\to A$ factors $(t_j)$. Any other factorization $w$ has $aw=v$, hence $w=baw=bv$. Thus $(U_{\mathcal C}A,q_j)$ is limiting. Together with steps 2–5, this proves creation, preservation and reflection of the finite limits claimed.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text: For clarity, when $I$ is empty, $L$ is terminal in $\mathcal C$. The three operations in step 2 are the unique maps to $L$ from $L\times L$, $*$ and $L$; every law is equality of two maps into $L$. Every $A$ has a unique underlying map to $L$, and its operation-preservation equations are likewise equalities into $L$. Thus the lifted group object is terminal, and the preceding proof includes the empty limit without assuming that $I$ is nonempty.

proof.text:
Now let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits. In particular $(F(X\times Y),F\mathrm{pr}_1,F\mathrm{pr}_2)$ is a product cone and $F(*)$ is terminal. Their universal properties give inverses $k_{X,Y}=\lambda_{X,Y}^{-1}:FX\times FY\to F(X\times Y)$ and $k_0=\lambda_*^{-1}:*_{\mathcal D}\to F(*)$. Each inverse identity follows by composing with both projections, or by terminal uniqueness. The same tests give, for $u:Z\to X$, $v:Z\to Y$, and $a:X\to X'$, $b:Y\to Y'$,
$$F\langle u,v\rangle=k_{X,Y}\langle Fu,Fv\rangle,\quad
F(a\times b)k_{X,Y}=k_{X',Y'}(Fa\times Fb),\quad
F(!_Z)=k_0!_{FZ}.$$
For example the projections of the first equality are $Fu,Fv$; those of the second are $Fa\,\mathrm{pr}_1,Fb\,\mathrm{pr}_2$. The third compares two maps into the terminal object $F(*)$.

proof.text:
On $FM$ define $\mu=F(m)k_{M,M}$, $\epsilon=F(e)k_0$, $\nu=F(i)$ as in the statement. Put $M^0=*$, $M^1=M$, and $M^{n+1}=M^n\times M$ for $n\geq1$, and similarly in $\mathcal D$. Define $\kappa_0=k_0$, $\kappa_1=1_{FM}$, $\kappa_{n+1}=k_{M^n,M}(\kappa_n\times1)$ for $n\geq1$. The projection equations in step 8 give $F(\mathrm{pr}_r)\kappa_n=\mathrm{pr}_r$ for every variable projection. For terms $t,s:M^n\to M$, let $\widetilde t,\widetilde s:(FM)^n\to FM$ be the corresponding composites using $\mu,\epsilon,\nu$. Starting with variables, substitution of the pairing identity in step 8 gives the three constructor calculations
$$\begin{aligned}
F(e!_{M^n})\kappa_n&=\epsilon!_{(FM)^n},\\
F(it)\kappa_n&=\nu(Ft\kappa_n),\\
F(m\langle t,s\rangle)\kappa_n&=F(m)k_{M,M}\langle Ft\kappa_n,Fs\kappa_n\rangle.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus whenever $Ft\kappa_n=\widetilde t$ and $Fs\kappa_n=\widetilde s$, these calculations give the same identity for their zero, inverse and sum terms. This is direct substitution in composites, not an appeal to a theorem about algebraic theories.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text: Apply the calculations of step 9 to the two sides of each defining group equation on $M$. For associativity take the terms $m\langle m\langle x,y\rangle,z\rangle$ and $m\langle x,m\langle y,z\rangle\rangle$ on $M^3$; both are equal, so applying $F$ and precomposing with $\kappa_3$ gives the associativity equation for $\mu$. For commutativity use $m\langle x,y\rangle=m\langle y,x\rangle$ on $M^2$ and $\kappa_2$. On $M^1=M$ the two unit equations use $m\langle e!_M,1\rangle=1=m\langle1,e!_M\rangle$, and the inverse equations use $m\langle1,i\rangle=e!_M=m\langle i,1\rangle$. Since $\kappa_1=1$, their images give both unit and both inverse laws for $\mu,\epsilon,\nu$. Hence the operations on $FM$ satisfy precisely every law required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text:
If $h:M\to N$ preserves the three operations, the naturality identity of step 8 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
Fh\,\mu_M&=F(hm_M)k_{M,M}=F(m_N(h\times h))k_{M,M}=\mu_N(Fh\times Fh),\\
Fh\,\epsilon_M&=F(he_M)k_0=F(e_N)k_0=\epsilon_N,\\
Fh\,\nu_M&=F(hi_M)=F(i_Nh)=\nu_NFh.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $h\mapsto Fh$ gives group-object morphisms. Identities and composition are preserved because $F$ preserves them, and group-object maps are determined by their underlying maps. Therefore this is the asserted functor $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$, with the literal underlying equality $U_{\mathcal D}F^{\mathrm{ab}}=FU_{\mathcal C}$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part and preceding quadruple discussion; explicit agent extraction of the finite-limit universal-property argument

proof.text: Finally take any limiting group-object cone over a finite diagram in $\operatorname{AbObj}(\mathcal C)$. By step 6 its underlying cone is limiting in $\mathcal C$. The hypothesis on $F$ makes its image limiting in $\mathcal D$. By step 11 this image is exactly the underlying cone of the $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$-image group cone, so the implication proved in step 5, now in $\mathcal D$, makes that group cone limiting. This proves preservation of every finite limit by $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$, including the empty one.
